messages.author: dbc3325e3846f67d
messages.subject: Logistic regression -- ROC
parts:
Dear all,

I'm using a Logistic Regression to do a classification task for binary
labels (1/0). As the model yields a prob of being in 1/0 category, i
still have to choose a threshold to transform the predicted
probabilities into binary 1 and 0. What I have now is a ROC Curve (x-
axis: 1-specificity, y-axis: sensitivity) but I have the slightest
idea how to choose the threshold still. Any thoughts?

Alvin

messages.author: cd4fa709cb39cadc
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Logistic regression -- ROC
parts:
>>As the model yields a prob of being in 1/0 category, i
still have to choose a threshold to transform the predicted
probabilities into binary 1 and 0

hi alvin,

couldn't you just take the sign of the logit-coefficients, such that negative values lead to 0 and positive ones to 1?

cheers,
daniel

messages.author: dbc3325e3846f67d
messages.subject: Re: Logistic regression -- ROC
parts:
Hi Daniel,

Yes it's possible but in that case the performance is not necessarily
the best. Besides, these binary category labels are imbalanced as
well, with the target category far less frequent. In the end, i want
to use the model i generated from the training data to do the
classification task in another set of testing data.

So the threshold probability for classifying an instance as 1 (target
category) has a lot to do with the model performance (precision/
recall). I know some use the threshold that makes the highest F-
measure. But still i'm wondering if there's any other way.

All the best,

alvin
